What happens to the flu virus when everyone and their grandmother's had it? Where does it go and how does it come back every year?
Where does the yearly new strain of the flu come from?

The flu changes itself in two major ways, Antigenic Drift and Antigenic Shift. Antigenic drift is what you are describing, and basically boils down to the fact that viruses are very primitive organisms, so when they replicate their DNA there are a lot of mistakes. Humans have multiple DNA repair mechanisms that minimize these mistakes in us. The flu mutates so rapidly that by the time the next flu season rolls around the virus has changed just enough to slip past the defenses we built for last year's flu. So it basically doesn't go anywhere, our defenses adapt to the current firm of the virus, but next year a slightly different presentation of the virus infects us, and the process repeats.

Not the parent, but as someone who loved both games, and pretty much thinks that HM2 is one of the best sequels I've seen in any medium (that wasn't part of a planned trilogy or whatever), I would strongly advise against playing HM2 first.

Hotline Miami is an incredibly tight and focused game that feels like a punch to the face. Shocking, exciting, and (perhaps disturbingly) addictive.

Hotline Miami 2 is a considered, methodical exploration of all the themes and mechanics of the first game, pushing every element of the game up to (and sometimes over) the breaking point. It fights dirty and expects you to do the same, and walking into it without the preparation provided by the first game is just setting yourself up for frustration.
